newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee called $150 up, may achieve $75.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee called $150 up, may achieve $75.

text.p: MAY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE robusta coffee futures are called to open Wednesday $150 higher after another strong New York performance on Tuesday, but traders said it might make an advance of $75.
On the charts the market, recovering from late-March lows, might have to do some work before progressing further, analysts said.
A move towards the $1,710 area might pave the way for more gains, but the market was unlikely to re-test $1,800, they said.
New York's arabica coffee futures bounced back from steep early losses to finish mostly higher in volatile trading Tuesday, boosted by chart-driven speculative and local buying.
May futures closed up 3.15 cents per lb, to 194.30 cents, after ranging from 195.00 to 183.50.
"It is clear that May is heading into a period of technical tightness, with roaster covering still needed against the contract," broker GNI said in a daily commentary.
"Fundamentally however, our prognosis of lower prices seems to be justified by the general level of physical demand for arabicas," it said.
"It is however good news for robustas, with roasters keen to maximise the input of cheaper coffee, which is leading to a mini demand-side boom," it added.
London robustas headed south on Tuesday as origin sellers returned from a long Easter break to unload their holdings.
Technically, the market had moved back into its current $1,600-$1,660 range after slipping to the reaction lows of $1,515 last week.
A break below $1,515 would take the market to the $1,450s, Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis said.
"At the moment, there are no signs it is going to do this."
The market has since rallied back to above $1,600 territory and Rigg said the market would have to do some more work before it could push up.
A push above the $1,710 area will possibly indicate further advances.
"However, the peak above $1,800 is unlikely to be taken out easily," she added.
